issues.title: Số câu hỏi không hợp lệ (0/100)
issues.description: Đề TOEIC Reading phải có đúng 100 câu được đánh dấu [QUESTION].

questions.prompt: If ------- are not satisfied with an item, return it for a full refund within 30 days of purchase.
questions.explanation: Chủ ngữ của mệnh đề "If ... are not satisfied" cần đại từ chủ ngữ: you.

questions.prompt: The location of next month’s online gaming forum is yet to be -------.
questions.explanation: Cụm "yet to be decided": chưa được quyết định (địa điểm được quyết định).

questions.prompt: Guests were ------- with the table decorations for the company banquet.
questions.explanation: Be impressed with: ấn tượng với. Chủ ngữ là người nên dùng V-ed.

questions.prompt: The Shubert Company is ------- effective at helping power plants reduce their carbon dioxide emissions.
questions.explanation: Very + tính từ (rất hiệu quả). "far" cần đi với so sánh hơn.

questions.prompt: Mr. Hodges ------- that volunteers sign up to assist with the Hannock River cleanup by Friday.
questions.explanation: Chủ ngữ số ít Mr. Hodges cần động từ chia hiện tại đơn: requests.

questions.prompt: Last year, the Daejeon English News ------- the number of readers by adding a digital subscription option.
questions.explanation: Last year nên dùng quá khứ; increased the number of readers: tăng lượng độc giả.

questions.prompt: Before the updated design can go into -------, it must be approved by management.
questions.explanation: Go into production: đi vào sản xuất. Sau giới từ cần danh từ.

questions.prompt: The economic development summit will be held ------- the Xi’an Trade Tower on September 22.
questions.explanation: Held at + địa điểm.

questions.prompt: Inclement weather was ------- responsible for the low turnout at Saturday’s Exton Music Festival.
questions.explanation: Trạng từ largely bổ nghĩa cho tính từ responsible: phần lớn chịu trách nhiệm.

questions.prompt: Our most recent survey was sent to clients just last week, ------- it is too soon to send another one.
questions.explanation: "so" nối vế chỉ kết quả: nên còn quá sớm để gửi khảo sát khác.

questions.prompt: ------- necklace that is shipped from Gillis Designers is given a thorough quality check.
questions.explanation: Each + danh từ đếm được số ít (necklace). "All" đi với danh từ số nhiều.

questions.prompt: Ms. Valdez’ sales numbers are good ------- for her to be considered for the employee-of-the-month award.
questions.explanation: Tính từ + enough + to V: đủ tốt để được xem xét.

questions.prompt: Aaron Park’s new book features photographs of homes designed and built by the homeowners -------.
questions.explanation: Đại từ phản thân quay về chủ thể số nhiều the homeowners: themselves.

questions.prompt: It is ------- for the audience to hold its applause until the speaker has finished.
questions.explanation: Customary: theo thông lệ, phù hợp nghĩa câu.

questions.prompt: Despite ------- that Legend Air would perform poorly with the entry of cheaper competition, it posted strong second-quarter earnings.
questions.explanation: Sau Despite cần danh từ; predictions that...: những dự đoán rằng...

questions.prompt: Mr. Nigam was ------- retirement when his boss asked him to be the head of security at the new facility.
questions.explanation: Close to retirement: gần đến lúc nghỉ hưu.

questions.prompt: Main Street Restaurant offers a menu of ------- prepared lunch and dinner meals.
questions.explanation: Trạng từ thoughtfully bổ nghĩa cho phân từ prepared.

questions.prompt: ------- our public relations manager, Ms. Ghazarian has just been appointed vice president of media relations.
questions.explanation: Formerly: trước đây là giám đốc PR, nay được bổ nhiệm vị trí mới.

questions.prompt: Videos of Korean pop music have become very popular ------- adolescents worldwide.
questions.explanation: Popular among + nhóm người: được ưa chuộng trong giới thanh thiếu niên.

questions.prompt: Milante Shoes ------- altered the firm’s marketing strategy after a recent economic shift.
questions.explanation: Trạng từ quickly bổ nghĩa cho động từ altered.

questions.prompt: The annual report has been posted online, ------- the director’s office has not yet received a printed copy.
questions.explanation: "but" nối hai vế đối lập: đã đăng online nhưng chưa nhận bản in.

questions.prompt: Hasin Fariz turned a study on the ------- effects of sleep into a best-selling book.
questions.explanation: Cần tính từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ effects: favorable (có lợi).

questions.prompt: Wynston Containers is ------- a yearly shutdown of its factory so that it can be evaluated for safety and efficiency.
questions.explanation: Implement a shutdown: thực hiện việc ngừng hoạt động hằng năm.

questions.prompt: The Girard Botanical Archive has almost 300,000 plant -------, all neatly pressed onto archival paper.
questions.explanation: Plant specimens: mẫu vật thực vật, được ép lên giấy lưu trữ.

questions.prompt: Hotels and universities are ------- to recycle their used mattresses through the city’s recycling program.
questions.explanation: Be eligible to V: đủ điều kiện làm gì.

questions.prompt: The ------- to review plans to replace the Tronton Bridge will be scheduled soon.
questions.explanation: Sau The cần danh từ: the hearing (buổi điều trần).

questions.prompt: Kovox Ltd. aims to optimize quality ------- reducing the impact on the environment.
questions.explanation: While + V-ing: trong khi (đồng thời) giảm tác động môi trường.

questions.prompt: The grocery store ------- vegetables from out of town until local prices went down last month.
questions.explanation: Hành động kéo dài đến một mốc trong quá khứ (last month): quá khứ hoàn thành tiếp diễn.

questions.prompt: All Hershel Industries employees must have a valid ID card ------- enter the building.
questions.explanation: In order to + V: để vào tòa nhà (chỉ mục đích).

questions.prompt: ------- and cost factored equally in choosing Cantavox as our main supplier.
questions.explanation: Reliability (độ tin cậy) đi cùng cost khi chọn nhà cung cấp.
Strive to V: nỗ lực làm gì.
For + khoảng thời gian (a combined total of 40 years).

options.B: We thank you for trusting in PGD Bank over these years.
options.C: We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.
options.D: Traffic on the boulevard has increased lately.

questions.explanation: Chi nhánh đóng cửa tạm thời, câu sau là "In the meantime..." nên phù hợp lời xin lỗi vì bất tiện.
Normal business hours: giờ làm việc bình thường.
Thư viết sau buổi gặp hôm nay, nói về cuộc trò chuyện đã diễn ra: quá khứ (enjoyed).
Ứng viên đã gặp nhà tuyển dụng, nên vòng cuối là interviews (phỏng vấn).
Tính từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ amount: substantial (đáng kể).

options.A: I have four additional questions to ask you.
options.B: I would be able to begin during the first week of February.
options.C: I am confident I have the potential for this position.
options.D: Thank you for the offer of employment.

questions.explanation: Câu trước nói về câu hỏi ngày bắt đầu làm việc, nên câu sau trả lời thời điểm có thể bắt đầu.

options.A: I can meet you when you arrive.
options.B: Scheduling flights can be quite tricky.
options.C: I have long admired your work on regional airports.
options.D: There are several dining options at the airport.

questions.explanation: Câu sau bắt đầu bằng "As a result, I am particularly eager to hear your ideas" nên câu trước nêu lý do: ngưỡng mộ công việc của ông Wu.
Tính từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ restaurants: excellent.
Join us: tham gia cùng chúng tôi (buổi gặp).
Appreciate + V-ing: discussing.
Liên hệ "begins on April 18" (tương lai): will run for five weeks.
Đây là liên hoan phim nên presenting movies from Asia and South America.
Popular event: sự kiện được nhiều người yêu thích (vé luôn bán hết nhanh).

options.A: The awards will be presented by Hunter Johns.
options.B: Renovations to the space are nearly complete.
options.C: The later offerings were an even bigger success.
options.D: Sales are open to the general public on March 3.

questions.explanation: Câu sau nói thành viên Film Club mua vé ưu tiên, nên câu này nêu thời điểm bán vé cho công chúng.

questions.prompt: For whom is the advertisement intended?
questions.explanation: Sự kiện tuyển dụng: nghe nhân viên chia sẻ, tìm hiểu vị trí, gặp nhà tuyển dụng, mang CV: dành cho người tìm việc.

questions.prompt: What is stated about Sedwick Electronics?

options.B: It offers a training program for new employees.
options.C: It requires employees to wear uniforms.
options.D: It will have more than one location.

questions.explanation: Công ty mở cơ sở mới ở Hanover và đã có cơ sở ở Lancaster: có nhiều hơn một địa điểm.

questions.prompt: What will happen on March 1?

options.B: A new policy will go into effect.
options.C: A promotional sale will take place.
options.D: A customer survey will be published.

questions.explanation: Từ March 1 khách được trả hàng mua online tại cửa hàng: chính sách mới có hiệu lực.

questions.prompt: What is NOT a requirement for a complete refund?

options.A: The return must be made at the original purchase location.
options.B: The return must be made within a certain time frame.
options.C: The item must be returned with all its components.
options.D: The item must be returned in the original packaging.

questions.explanation: Điều kiện gồm: trong 30 ngày, có biên lai, bao bì gốc, đủ linh kiện. Không yêu cầu trả tại nơi mua gốc.

questions.prompt: Why would people enroll in the course taught by Ms. Sanders?

options.C: To get tips on creating spreadsheets
options.D: To learn how to advertise on the Internet

questions.explanation: Bà Sanders dạy khóa Spreadsheet Basics: học cách tạo bảng tính và biểu đồ.

questions.prompt: What is indicated about Ms. Farid?

options.D: She used to work as a data analyst.

questions.explanation: Bà Farid dạy lớp thứ Bảy (Internet Safety) và Chủ nhật (Spreadsheet Basics): hai buổi mỗi tuần.

questions.prompt: Why did Ms. Witham contact Ms. Ohara?

options.D: To determine the most convenient train to take

questions.explanation: Hai người bàn cách đến, giờ bắt đầu chuyến thăm lúc 2:00: sắp xếp chuyến thăm cửa hàng.

questions.prompt: At 4:51 P.M., what does Ms. Ohara most likely mean when she writes, “You should like things here, too”?

options.A: The Tokyo store is being run according to corporate policy.
options.B: Ms. Witham will find the athletic shoes she needs.
options.C: Ms. Ohara’s associate is always punctual.
options.D: The Tokyo store is located next to a popular restaurant.

questions.explanation: Sally khen cửa hàng Kyoto đạt đúng tiêu chuẩn của trụ sở; Ohara đáp "cũng sẽ thích ở đây": cửa hàng Tokyo cũng vận hành theo chính sách công ty.

questions.prompt: What did Ms. Tulio most likely do?
questions.explanation: Báo cáo đánh giá tình trạng từng bộ phận cầu: bà Tulio đã thực hiện kiểm tra.

questions.prompt: What part of the structure is in most need of maintenance?
questions.explanation: Mặt đường (Road surface) có điểm thấp nhất là 3, nghĩa là xuống cấp nhất.

questions.prompt: What is probably true about the Blaine River Drawbridge?

options.A: It was not designed for pedestrian use.
options.B: It will be closed for the month of October.
options.C: It does not have the required signage.
options.D: It is the oldest bridge on the Ridgeline Highway.

questions.explanation: Sidewalk or walkway được chấm 6 (Not applicable): cầu không có lối đi bộ.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the article?

options.A: To clarify where subway riders can locate information
options.B: To describe improvements at some subway stations
options.C: To announce the creation of a new subway line
options.D: To explain why subway schedules will be revised

questions.explanation: Bài báo thông báo việc nâng cấp hệ thống loa thông báo ở một số ga tàu điện.

questions.prompt: How does Mr. Miller feel about the plans?

options.A: He expects the project to fail.
options.B: He is concerned about the cost.
options.C: He believes the work is unnecessary.
options.D: He has been waiting for the changes.

questions.explanation: Ông Miller nói "it is about time!": đã chờ thay đổi này từ lâu.

questions.prompt: The word “stages” in paragraph 5, line 2, is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Came together in stages: hình thành theo từng giai đoạn, tức steps.

questions.prompt: What is indicated about Datoric Systems?

options.A: It has increased the spending amount allowed for business dinners.
options.B: It will adopt new procedures for filing travel expense reports.
options.C: It has office locations in several countries.
options.D: It plans to hold a company celebration.

questions.explanation: Thư mở đầu bằng "several new procedures regarding business trip expense reports": công ty áp dụng quy trình mới.

questions.prompt: Why is the accounting software mentioned?

options.A: To highlight a special capability it has
options.B: To encourage staff to install it
options.C: To help employees log on to it
options.D: To point out that it will be replaced

questions.explanation: Phần mềm sẽ tự động tính tổng số tiền được hoàn: nhấn mạnh một tính năng đặc biệt.

questions.prompt: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? “Following these steps will enable us to quickly issue your reimbursement payment.”
questions.explanation: Câu "Following these steps" đứng sau phần liệt kê các quy định cần làm theo, tức vị trí [2].

questions.prompt: What is the main topic of the article?

options.A: New trends in marketing athletic footwear
options.B: Increased competition in the African clothing market
options.C: Recent growth in the African fashion industry
options.D: The largest clothing companies in Africa

questions.explanation: Toàn bài nói về sự phát triển của ngành thời trang châu Phi nhờ thương mại điện tử.

questions.prompt: What is indicated about Abbi Sportscore?

options.A: It sells its products only online.
options.B: It manufactures its shoes in Nazret.
options.C: It will be moving its main offices soon.
options.D: It was the first shoe company in Ethiopia.

questions.explanation: Bà Absher nhấn mạnh lợi thế sản xuất sản phẩm tại thành phố quê hương Nazret.

questions.prompt: What is suggested about the Jumjum and Longa Web sites?

options.B: They receive orders from around the world.
options.C: They offer free shipping to London and New York.
options.D: They are planning to open retail stores.

questions.explanation: Hai trang web đưa hàng thiết kế châu Phi đến tận London và New York: nhận đơn từ khắp thế giới.

questions.prompt: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3], and [4] does the following sentence best belong? “The city boasts four garment factories, with a fifth scheduled to be built this year in nearby Wonji.”
questions.explanation: Câu nói về "the city" có nhà máy may nên đứng ngay sau câu nhắc đến thành phố Nazret, tức vị trí [3].

questions.prompt: Where do the people most likely work?
questions.explanation: Họ bàn về cover design của số tháng 9 và tiêu đề bài viết: nhà xuất bản tạp chí.

questions.prompt: Why does Mr. Park apologize?

options.B: He used an old e-mail address.

questions.explanation: Ông Park quên và gửi nhầm bản cũ, sau đó gửi lại bản mới nhất.

questions.prompt: At 10:30 A.M., what does Ms. Riley most likely mean when she writes, “That’s more like it”?
questions.explanation: Bà Riley yêu cầu nền sáng hơn; mở bản mới và hài lòng: màu trông đẹp hơn.

questions.prompt: What will Mr. Ojeda do by the afternoon?
questions.explanation: Ông Ojeda sẽ có bản in sẵn sau bữa trưa: làm bản in mẫu.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the letter?

options.A: To seek volunteers for an event

questions.explanation: Thư mở đầu: bà Chelvi được đề cử vào vòng chung kết cuộc thi.

questions.prompt: What does Ms. Chelvi most likely specialize in?
questions.explanation: Bà đã phát triển một ứng dụng web: lĩnh vực công nghệ.

questions.prompt: The word “illustrates” in paragraph 3, line 2, is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Video "illustrates the use of your application": thể hiện, minh họa cách dùng, gần nghĩa represents.

questions.prompt: What is Ms. Chelvi asked to do by March 10?
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3 liệt kê tài liệu phải nộp trước 10 tháng 3, trong đó có ký biểu mẫu đồng ý.

questions.prompt: According to the e-mail, how did Mr. Riedewald receive reward points?

options.B: He participated in a customer survey.
options.C: He spent a certain amount of money.

questions.explanation: Thư cảm ơn ông đã điền khảo sát nên cộng điểm thưởng.

questions.prompt: In the e-mail, the phrase “filling out” in paragraph 1, line 1, is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Fill out a survey: điền (hoàn thành) bảng khảo sát, gần nghĩa completing.

questions.prompt: How can customers apply their reward points in an MHF retail store?

options.C: By scanning a coupon’s bar code
options.D: By going to the Client Services Department

questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: in phiếu giảm giá có mã vạch và quét tại quầy thanh toán.

questions.prompt: According to the receipt, what is true about Mr. Riedewald?

options.A: He paid for delivery of the items.
options.B: He purchased the items in the evening.
options.C: He paid over $70 for all items combined.
options.D: He purchased only one item at regular price.

questions.explanation: Trên hóa đơn chỉ có Floral Blanket (25.00) không bị giảm giá; phí giao hàng miễn phí, mua lúc 11:31 A.M., tổng 62.00.

questions.prompt: What item did Mr. Riedewald most likely purchase using reward credits?
questions.explanation: Điểm thưởng hiện trên hóa đơn dưới dạng "Special Discount", không dùng cho hàng thanh lý hoặc từ $15 trở lên: khung ảnh (10.00).

questions.prompt: What is a purpose of the letter?

options.A: To ask Mr. Morello to write a book
options.C: To notify Mr. Morello of a payment
options.D: To describe an updated personnel policy

questions.explanation: Câu đầu: "Enclosed please find your royalty payment": thông báo về khoản thanh toán tiền nhuận bút.

questions.prompt: What was sent in a previous message to Mr. Morello?

options.D: A link to an electronic book

questions.explanation: Email trước đó đã liệt kê số liệu bán hàng (sales figures) và tiền nhuận bút.

questions.prompt: What does Ms. Wicklin mention about Two Swan Press?

options.A: It moved to a new location in October.
options.B: It has launched a new program for its fifth anniversary.
options.C: It has won an industry award.
options.D: It has decided to focus on scientific publications.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: nhà xuất bản nhận giải Publisher of the Year từ ngành sách Anh.

questions.prompt: What is suggested about Mr. Booth?

options.A: He is a Two Swan Press author.
options.B: He wrote Business in Our Lives.
options.C: He is an acquaintance of Mr. Morello.
options.D: He has purchased items from Two Swan Press before.

questions.explanation: Mã AUX1417 chỉ dành cho tác giả, mà tác giả cuốn sách ông Booth mua là Schuyler: nhiều khả năng ông Booth quen ông Morello và được dùng mã.

questions.prompt: What is indicated about the order?

options.B: It has not yet been paid.

questions.explanation: Ưu đãi tháng 12 miễn phí vận chuyển đơn trên £35; đơn này £45.

questions.prompt: What does the e-mail indicate about the mentoring program?

options.B: The number of participants is limited.
options.C: It is designed for staff in the sales division.
options.D: Participants must attend an orientation meeting.

questions.explanation: Email nêu "a maximum of ten junior employees": số người tham gia có giới hạn.

questions.prompt: How will the junior employees most likely be selected?

options.A: They will be chosen from a management-training group.
options.C: They will be evaluated by Mr. Wrigley.
options.D: They will be recommended by a local business school.

questions.explanation: Ứng viên nộp đơn cho ông Wrigley và ông sẽ thông báo "his selections": ông Wrigley đánh giá, lựa chọn.

questions.prompt: What is suggested about Ms. Drummond?

options.A: She has worked at Broadside Electronics for less than eighteen months.
options.B: She has just transferred from another department.
options.C: She has received a positive annual review.
options.D: She has made many successful presentations abroad.

questions.explanation: Chương trình chỉ dành cho nhân viên dưới 18 tháng, bà Drummond đã được nhận: làm việc dưới 18 tháng.

questions.prompt: What is most likely true about Ms. Russo?

options.A: She is planning to retire soon.
options.C: She has mentored many junior employees.
options.D: She recently joined the hiring team.

questions.explanation: Bà Russo là phó chủ tịch kinh doanh và được ghép với Drummond vì Drummond muốn học về thị trường nước ngoài: bà có kinh nghiệm bán hàng quốc tế.

questions.prompt: What benefit from the mentoring program have both Ms. Drummond and Ms. Russo enjoyed?
questions.explanation: Russo "more satisfied with my own duties", Drummond "a happier person when I arrive to work": cả hai hài lòng công việc hơn.

questions.prompt: What does the Web site indicate about fences taller than three meters?

options.B: They are usually prohibited by law.
options.D: They must be ordered directly from the manufacturer.

questions.explanation: Quy định địa phương thường chỉ cho phép tối đa 3 mét: hàng rào cao hơn thường bị luật cấm.

questions.prompt: According to the form, why does Ms. Carhart need a temporary fence installed?

options.B: To draw attention to an exhibit
options.C: To control a crowd at a special event
options.D: To limit public access to a work site

questions.explanation: Mẫu ghi: ngăn công chúng vào trong thời gian cải tạo: hạn chế người ngoài vào khu vực thi công.

questions.prompt: What information does Ms. Carhart fail to give about the fence she needs?

options.A: The height of the fence to be erected
options.B: The dates when the fence is needed
options.C: The perimeter of the area to be enclosed

questions.explanation: Cô đã nêu chiều cao 3 mét, ngày 18 đến 30 tháng 8, hai cổng; chưa nêu chu vi khu vực cần rào.

questions.prompt: What is implied about Ms. Carhart’s fence project?

options.A: There will be a charge for delivery.
options.B: The project involves work at several job sites.
options.C: Extra workers must be hired to install the fence.
options.D: Inspectors must first approve the project.

questions.explanation: Cô cần hàng rào trong vòng 2 tuần (dưới 3 tuần): đơn gấp nên bị tính phí giao hàng.

questions.prompt: Why does Mr. Montalbo recommend adding a curtain?

options.A: It would act as a noise barrier.
options.B: It would help keep in dust.
options.C: It would serve as a visual screen.

questions.explanation: Tấm màn nhựa che công trường khỏi tầm nhìn của người đi bộ: tấm chắn thị giác.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.

Employees who have been with Broadside Electronics for less than eighteen months are invited to apply to participate in a new mentoring program that will match a maximum of ten junior employees with long-term company veterans. The goal is that junior employees will sharpen corporate skills, better understand company culture, and develop a more focused career path. Mentees will be assigned to a mentor based strictly on their work assignment and professional interests. The pairs will meet at mutually convenient times throughout the year, from three to five hours per month.
To be considered for participation in this initiative, complete the attached application and return to Mentoring Program Director Tim Wrigley at t.wrigley@broadsideelec.com by July 1. Mr. Wrigley will send notification of his selections by July 15.

The Broadside Company Newsletter
Mentoring Program Sees Results
Long-time employee and Vice President of Sales Alena Russo was intrigued when a Personnel Department director approached her about mentoring a less experienced employee under a program that began last year. She is glad to have accepted the assignment. “After working with Ms. Drummond, I am more satisfied with my own duties, because I know I have helped a professional who is just getting started. I only wish that I had had someone looking out for me in my early years,” remarked Ms. Russo.
Ms. Drummond explains that she “needed pointers on how to make better sales pitches.” She reports that her sales are up by 20 percent now. She better understands the opportunities Broadside Electronics has to offer and what is required to become a manager. “Thanks to Ms. Russo, I have been able to define my career goals, and I am a happier person when I arrive to work every day.”
New mentorship pairs are now being formed. Interested parties should contact Tim Wrigley in the Personnel Department.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.
[/PASSAGE]

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.
[/PASSAGE]

Dear PGD Account Holder,

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.

Subway Sound to be Upgraded
BOSTON (April 1)—The public address systems at selected subway stations are scheduled to be refurbished, the Transit Authority announced this week. The systems are used to make announcements to commuters both on the platforms and in the stations.
Local commuters welcomed the news, although for some it was long overdue.
“It can be pretty difficult to understand the announcements at some of the stations I use most frequently,” said Ian Miller, who has taken the subway to work nearly every week for the past eighteen years. “I had heard the reports about it on TV, and all I can say is that it is about time!”
Some of the systems currently in use are more than 30 years old. Worn-out speakers, wiring, microphones, and amplifiers will be replaced with new, more reliable devices. The work should be completed in October and cost more than $11 million.
Boston’s subway system came together in stages over the course of several years. The foundational component of the system’s Green Line first opened on Tremont Street in the late 1890s. It was the first of its kind in the United States.

E-Commerce Opening Doors for African Fashion Industry
ADDIS ABABA (6 May)—Africa’s role as a consumer of fashion has been on the rise in recent years. This trend is largely due to the emergence of e-commerce, which provides Africans the opportunity to buy clothing from retailers with no physical presence on the continent.
Perhaps more importantly, though, the growth of e-commerce is enabling small-scale African designers to also become producers of fashion, as they showcase their collections to consumers worldwide. African shopping Web sites like Jumjum and Longa are making the work of African designers available for purchase not just throughout the continent, but also as far away as London and New York. — [1] —.
“African designers are finally gaining visibility,” says Mazaa Absher, founder of Abbi Sportscore, Africa’s fastest-growing athletic footwear company. “We have always had terrific design and production capacity here on the continent, but it was hard getting it out into the world. Now we are generating more sales online than we are in our stores.” — [2] —.
Even as Ms. Absher has transformed her company into an international powerhouse, she continues to highlight the advantages of manufacturing its products in her home city of Nazret. — [3] —. Africa’s strong textile sector and innovative designs combine tradition and wearability, and this formula is allowing companies like hers to set their sights beyond the continent.
“As more cities in Ethiopia—and all over Africa—improve their manufacturing capacity, it will become easier to reach the rest of the world,” says Ms. Absher. — [4] —.
